R_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})=\sum_{p}n_{T}(p)\sum_{t:p_{t}=p}\frac{1}{n_{T}(p)}\|\rho^{p}_{T}-y_{t}\|^{2}_{2}~,\quad K_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})=\sum_{p}{n_{T}(p)}\|p-\rho^{p}_{T}\|^{2}_{2}~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_example">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Example 2.3</span></span><span id="S2.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Denote the Shannon entropy under distribution <math id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> to be <math id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="H(p)=-\sum_{k}p_{k}\log p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.055em">−</mo><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>log</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(p)=-\sum_{k}p_{k}\log p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. For <em id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">log loss</em> <math id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\ell(p,y)=-\sum^{K}_{k=1}y_{k}\log p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.055em">−</mo><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>log</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(p,y)=-\sum^{K}_{k=1}y_{k}\log p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>,
the refinement score
equals the weighted sum of the Shannon entropy within each bin, and the calibration error becomes the
KL–calibration <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx18" title="" class="ltx_ref">LSS25</a>]</cite>,</p>
<table id="S2.EGx5" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S2.Ex5"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle R_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})=\sum_{p}n_{T}(p)H(\rho^{p}_{T})~,\quad K_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})=\sum_{p}{n_{T}(p)}\,\mathrm{KL}(\rho^{p}_{T}\|p)~." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>p</mi></munder></mstyle><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.330em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>p</mi></munder></mstyle><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>p</mi><mo rspace="0.052em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle R_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})=\sum_{p}n_{T}(p)H(\rho^{p}_{T})~,\quad K_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})=\sum_{p}{n_{T}(p)}\,\mathrm{KL}(\rho^{p}_{T}\|p)~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Motivated by this decomposition, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx8" title="" class="ltx_ref">FH23</a>]</cite> compare the learner to the external forecaster’s refinement score and define the notions of <em id="S2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">calibeating</em> and <em id="S2.p6.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">multi-calibeating</em>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 2.4</span></span><span id="S2.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Calibeating and Multi-Calibeating)<span id="S2.Thmtheorem4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A learner
is <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(T)</annotation></semantics></math>-<em id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">multi-calibeating</em> w.r.t. loss <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> if for any
external forecasts <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\{q^{(n)}_{1:T}\}^{N}_{n=1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{q^{(n)}_{1:T}\}^{N}_{n=1}</annotation></semantics></math> and outcomes
<math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="y_{1:T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{1:T}</annotation></semantics></math>, the learner’s predictions <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{1:T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1:T}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy</p>
<table id="S2.EGx6" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S2.E1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle L_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})\leq R_{T}(q^{(n)}_{1:T},y_{1:T})+\alpha(T)~,\forall n\in[N]~." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo rspace="0.330em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo rspace="0.052em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle L_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})\leq R_{T}(q^{(n)}_{1:T},y_{1:T})+\alpha(T)~,\forall n\in[N]~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We call <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(T)</annotation></semantics></math> the multi-calibeating rate.
We say the learner is multi-calibeating if <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(T)=o(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(T)=o(T)</annotation></semantics></math>.
When (<a href="#S2.E1" title="Eq. 1 ‣ Definition 2.4 (Calibeating and Multi-Calibeating). ‣ 2 Model ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) holds in expectation over the learner’s randomness, we call <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(T)</annotation></semantics></math> the expected multi-calibeating rate.
When there is only <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=1</annotation></semantics></math> external forecast, we simply say calibeating.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">We also introduce another performance measure called calibration.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 2.5</span></span><span id="S2.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Calibration)<span id="S2.Thmtheorem5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A learner is <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta(T)</annotation></semantics></math>-calibrated w.r.t. loss <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> if for any outcome sequences <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="y_{1:T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{1:T}</annotation></semantics></math> (and any external forecasts),
the learner’s predictions <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{1:T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1:T}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy</p>
<table id="S2.EGx7" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S2.E2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle K_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})\leq\beta(T)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>β</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle K_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})\leq\beta(T).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We call <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta(T)</annotation></semantics></math> the calibration rate and say the algorithm is calibrated if <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta(T)=o(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta(T)=o(T)</annotation></semantics></math>.
When (<a href="#S2.E2" title="Eq. 2 ‣ Definition 2.5 (Calibration). ‣ 2 Model ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) holds in expectation over the algorithm’s randomness, we call <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta(T)</annotation></semantics></math> the expected calibration rate.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Note that calibeating and calibration are incomparable in general.
Calibeating only guarantees that the learner’s loss is no larger than the forecaster’s loss minus the forecaster’s calibration error, i.e., it competes with the <em id="S2.p8.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">external forecaster</em>’s refinement score.
The learner’s calibration error might not vanish if
it itself attains a low refinement term.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Calibeating <math id="S3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>=</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=</annotation></semantics></math> No-Regret Learning</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section considers the calibeating problem, i.e., when there is only one external forecast every round.
Let <math id="S3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q\coloneqq\{q_{t}:t\in[T]\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q\coloneqq\{q_{t}:t\in[T]\}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the set of distinct external forecast values that appear over the horizon.<span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
            
            
            
            
            
            
            
          We also use <math id="footnote1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> to denote the set of possible external forecast values for lower bound results.</span></span></span>
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx8" title="" class="ltx_ref">FH23</a>]</cite> study the Brier and log losses and give algorithms
with calibeating rate of <math id="S3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(|Q|\log T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(|Q|\log T)</annotation></semantics></math>.
We recover and extend their results by reductions to no-regret learning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">First, define the regret of predictions <math id="S3.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{1:T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1:T}</annotation></semantics></math> under outcomes <math id="S3.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="y_{1:T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{1:T}</annotation></semantics></math> to be</p>
<table id="S3.EGx8" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex6"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})\coloneqq\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})-\min_{p\in\Delta_{K}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p,y_{t})~." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Reg</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≔</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover></mstyle><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover></mstyle><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.052em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})\coloneqq\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})-\min_{p\in\Delta_{K}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p,y_{t})~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">We say an algorithm has (expected-)regret of <math id="S3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(T)</annotation></semantics></math> if <math id="S3.p2.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{Reg}_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})\leq\alpha(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Reg</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>α</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Reg}_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})\leq\alpha(T)</annotation></semantics></math> always holds (in expectation).
The following theorem shows that calibeating reduces to no-regret learning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 3.1</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any proper loss <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> and any online algorithm <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖠</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> with regret <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(T)</annotation></semantics></math>,
where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> is a concave function, <a href="#algorithm1" title="In 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> is <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|Q|\alpha(T/|Q|)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|Q|\alpha(T/|Q|)</annotation></semantics></math>-calibeating.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">The reduction partitions the rounds <math id="S3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[T]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[T]</annotation></semantics></math> by the external forecast value <math id="S3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, and runs an independent copy of the no-regret learner <math id="S3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖠</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> for each forecast value.
Formally,
for any external forecast <math id="S3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> that appeared at least once, run a separate copy of <math id="S3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖠</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}</annotation></semantics></math>, denoted as <math id="S3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝖠</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}_{q}</annotation></semantics></math>, on the subset of rounds <math id="S3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}_{q}\coloneq\{t:q_{t}=q\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}_{q}\coloneq\{t:q_{t}=q\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For each subsequence, we have</span></p>
<table id="S3.EGx9" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex7"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\sum_{t:q_{t}=q}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})-\min_{p\in\Delta_{K}}\sum_{t:q_{t}=q}\ell(p,y_{t})\leq\alpha(n_{T}(q))~." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>α</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.052em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\sum_{t:q_{t}=q}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})-\min_{p\in\Delta_{K}}\sum_{t:q_{t}=q}\ell(p,y_{t})\leq\alpha(n_{T}(q))~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Summing up over all the subsequences and by <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1" title="Definition 2.1. ‣ 2 Model ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Definition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>, we have</span></p>
<table id="S3.EGx10" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex8"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle L_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})-R_{T}(q_{1:T},y_{1:T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle L_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})-R_{T}(q_{1:T},y_{1:T})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\leq\sum_{q}\alpha(n_{T}(q))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>q</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\leq\sum_{q}\alpha(n_{T}(q))</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.Ex9"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\leq|Q|\alpha\left(\frac{\sum_{q}n_{T}(q)}{|Q|}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>q</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\leq|Q|\alpha\left(\frac{\sum_{q}n_{T}(q)}{|Q|}\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(Jensen’s inequality)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.Ex10"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=|Q|\alpha\left(\frac{T}{|Q|}\right)~," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo rspace="0.330em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=|Q|\alpha\left(\frac{T}{|Q|}\right)~,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">which finishes the proof.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
<div id="S3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We note that common regret bounds obtained for standard online algorithms are all concave in <math id="S3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, e.g., they are often of the form <math id="S3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O((\log T)^{\alpha}T^{\beta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>α</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>β</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O((\log T)^{\alpha}T^{\beta})</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="S3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\in[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\in[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>. The algorithm of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx8" title="" class="ltx_ref">FH23</a>]</cite> can be recovered as a special case of <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>, with the online algorithm being  <span title="" class="ltx_glossaryref ltx_missing">FTL</span> (<abbr title="" class="ltx_glossaryref ltx_missing">FTL</abbr>) (with a standard interior restriction for the log loss to avoid the unbounded boundary).
Moreover, <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> readily obtains <math id="S3.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\sqrt{|Q|KT})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\sqrt{|Q|KT})</annotation></semantics></math> for bounded proper losses <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx17" title="" class="ltx_ref">LSS24</a>]</cite> and <math id="S3.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(|Q|\log T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(|Q|\log T)</annotation></semantics></math> for mixable losses <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx14" title="" class="ltx_ref">HAK07</a>]</cite>, which encompasses Brier and log losses as special cases.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 3.2</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For bounded proper loss <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, instantiating the online learner in <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> with the follow-the-perturbed-leader algorithm of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx17" title="" class="ltx_ref">LSS24</a>]</cite> yields an algorithm with expected calibeating rate of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\sqrt{|Q|KT})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\sqrt{|Q|KT})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p6.1" class="ltx_p">We note that, inherited from the no-regret guarantees in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx17" title="" class="ltx_ref">LSS24</a>]</cite>, the algorithm in <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Corollary 3.2. ‣ 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> can actually achieve <math id="S3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\sqrt{|Q|KT})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\sqrt{|Q|KT})</annotation></semantics></math> <em id="S3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">simultaneously</em> for all bounded proper losses.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 3.3</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A convex function <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>-mixable if for any probability distribution <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi\in\Delta(\Delta_{K})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi\in\Delta(\Delta_{K})</annotation></semantics></math>, there exists a prediction <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\pi}\in\Delta_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\pi}\in\Delta_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> such that
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{-\eta\ell(p_{\pi},y)}\geq\int e^{-\eta\ell(p,y)}\pi(\mathrm{d}p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>π</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo rspace="0.111em">≥</mo><mrow><mo>∫</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-\eta\ell(p_{\pi},y)}\geq\int e^{-\eta\ell(p,y)}\pi(\mathrm{d}p)</annotation></semantics></math> holds for all <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y\in\mathcal{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\in\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 3.4</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For an <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>-mixable loss <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., Brier and log losses), instantiating the online learner in <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> with  <span title="" class="ltx_glossaryref ltx_missing">EWOO</span> (<abbr title="" class="ltx_glossaryref ltx_missing">EWOO</abbr>) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx14" title="" class="ltx_ref">HAK07</a>]</cite> yields an algorithm with expected calibeating rate of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(|Q|\log T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(|Q|\log T)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Besides the upper bound, we also prove that any lower bound for no-regret learning with a proper loss implies a lower bound for calibeating.
Combining with <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>, our results show that calibeating is minimax-equivalent to regret minimization. We defer the proof to <a href="#A1.SS1" title="A.1 Proof of ‣ Appendix A Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 3.5</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any proper loss <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, denote the optimal regret bound as</span></p>
<table id="S3.EGx11" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\beta(T)\coloneqq\inf_{\mathsf{A}}\sup_{y_{1:T}\in\mathcal{E}^{T}}\mathbb{E}_{p_{1:T}\sim\mathsf{A}}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell\left(p_{t},y_{t}\right)-\min_{p\in\Delta_{K}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell\left(p,y_{t}\right)\right]~," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">≔</mo><munder><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0.0835em">inf</mo><mi>𝖠</mi></munder><munder><mo lspace="0.0835em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">sup</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∼</mo><mi>𝖠</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover></mstyle><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover></mstyle><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.330em">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\beta(T)\coloneqq\inf_{\mathsf{A}}\sup_{y_{1:T}\in\mathcal{E}^{T}}\mathbb{E}_{p_{1:T}\sim\mathsf{A}}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell\left(p_{t},y_{t}\right)-\min_{p\in\Delta_{K}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell\left(p,y_{t}\right)\right]~,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖠</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> ranges over (possibly randomized) online algorithms.
Then, every algorithm is at best <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|Q|\beta(\lfloor T/|Q|\rfloor)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌊</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌋</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|Q|\beta(\lfloor T/|Q|\rfloor)</annotation></semantics></math>-calibeating.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Combining <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 3.5. ‣ 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a> with known regret lower bounds for bounded proper losses <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx17" title="" class="ltx_ref">LSS24</a>]</cite> and Brier and log losses <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx5" title="" class="ltx_ref">CL06</a>]</cite> yields the following.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 3.6</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There exist bounded proper losses
with calibeating rate
at least <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega(\sqrt{|Q|KT})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega(\sqrt{|Q|KT})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 3.7</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For the Brier and log losses, the calibeating rate is at least <math id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega(|Q|\log(T/|Q|))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega(|Q|\log(T/|Q|))</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Multi-Calibeating <math id="S4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>=</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=</annotation></semantics></math> Calibeating <math id="S4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math> Expert Problem</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Next, we consider the multi-calibeating problem.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx8" title="" class="ltx_ref">FH23</a>]</cite> obtain multi-calibeating rates of <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O((N+|Q|)\log T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O((N+|Q|)\log T)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\sqrt{NT}+|Q|\log T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\sqrt{NT}+|Q|\log T)</annotation></semantics></math>, via Blackwell approachability and online linear regression.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee+22</a>]</cite> achieve a rate logarithmic in <math id="S4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>, but polynomial in <math id="S4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> (more precisely, <math id="S4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\smash{\tilde{O}(\sqrt{|Q|}(\log N)^{\frac{1}{4}}T^{\frac{3}{4}})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>O</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{\tilde{O}(\sqrt{|Q|}(\log N)^{\frac{1}{4}}T^{\frac{3}{4}})}</annotation></semantics></math> for the optimal choice of parameters).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This section presents a simple reduction from multi-calibeating to the expert problem.
Via that reduction, we achieve the optimal multi-calibeating rates.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Expert Problem.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The interaction protocol in this problem is the same as in multi-calibeating: at each round <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the learner observes <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> expert predictions <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\smash{\{p_{t}^{(n)}\}_{n}\subseteq\Delta_{K}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{\{p_{t}^{(n)}\}_{n}\subseteq\Delta_{K}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and makes its own prediction <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}\in\Delta_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}\in\Delta_{K}</annotation></semantics></math>.
An experts algorithm <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖤</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{E}</annotation></semantics></math>
achieves regret <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma(T)</annotation></semantics></math> if for every sequence
<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\smash{\{(p_{t}^{(1:N)},y_{t})\}_{t=1}^{T}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{\{(p_{t}^{(1:N)},y_{t})\}_{t=1}^{T}}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S4.EGx12" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.E4"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})\right]\leq\min_{n\in[N]}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p_{t}^{(n)},y_{t})+\gamma(T)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mmultiscripts><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><mprescripts></mprescripts><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow></mmultiscripts></mstyle><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})\right]\leq\min_{n\in[N]}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p_{t}^{(n)},y_{t})+\gamma(T),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the expectation is over the randomness of <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖤</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{E}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Comparing this definition of regret with the definition of multi-calibeating rate, the only difference is that the latter remaps the experts/forecasters’ predictions optimally, while the former does not.
The remapping of each individual forecaster is precisely the problem of calibeating.
Hence, we run a separate calibeating algorithm for each forecaster, and use an experts algorithm to aggregate their decision.
See <a href="#algorithm2" title="In Expert Problem. ‣ 4 Multi-Calibeating = Calibeating + Expert Problem ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> for a formal description.</p>
</div>
<figure id="algorithm2" class="ltx_float ltx_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="algorithm2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 2</span> </span>Multicalibeating by Expert Aggregation</figcaption>
<div id="algorithm2.4" class="ltx_listing ltx_lst_numbers_left ltx_framed ltx_framed_topbottom ltx_listing">
<div id="algorithm2.4.1" class="ltx_listingline">
<span id="algorithm2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Sub-routines:</span>
</div>
<div id="algorithm2.4.2" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm2.4.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1</span></span>
            [.5ex]

<ul id="S4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I1.1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S4.I1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">4</span></span> 
<div id="S4.I1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">[after=</p>
<p id="S4.I1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">,parsep=0pt]</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each forecaster <math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in[N]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in[N]</annotation></semantics></math>, a separate calibeating algorithm <math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{(n)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{(n)}</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#algorithm1" title="In 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;padding-top:0.0pt;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S4.I1.i2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">5</span></span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Experts algorithm <math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖤</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{E}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx10" title="" class="ltx_ref">FS97</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm2.4.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2</span></span>
            
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm2.4.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3</span></span>
            <span id="algorithm2.4.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span> <em id="algorithm2.4.2.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic"><math id="algorithm2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="algorithm2.4.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_upright">to</span> <math id="algorithm2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math></em> <span id="algorithm2.4.2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">do</span>
</div>
<div id="algorithm2.4.3" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> <span id="algorithm2.4.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">// </span><span id="algorithm2.4.3.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">prediction </span>
</div>
<div id="algorithm2.4.4" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm2.4.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">4</span></span>
            Observe external forecasts <math id="algorithm2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}^{(1)},\dots,q_{t}^{(N)}\in\Delta_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}^{(1)},\dots,q_{t}^{(N)}\in\Delta_{K}</annotation></semantics></math>.
</div>
<div id="algorithm2.4.5" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm2.4.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">5</span></span>
            For each <math id="algorithm2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in[N]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in[N]</annotation></semantics></math>, query <math id="algorithm2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{(n)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{(n)}</annotation></semantics></math> with forecast <math id="algorithm2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}^{(n)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}^{(n)}</annotation></semantics></math> to get its prediction <math id="algorithm2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}^{(n)}\in\Delta_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}^{(n)}\in\Delta_{K}</annotation></semantics></math>.
</div>
<div id="algorithm2.4.6" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm2.4.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">6</span></span>
            Query <math id="algorithm2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖤</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{E}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="algorithm2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{p_{t}^{(n)}\}_{n=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{p_{t}^{(n)}\}_{n=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> as the experts’ forecasts, and follow its prediction <math id="algorithm2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. 
</div>
<div id="algorithm2.4.7" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm2.4.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">7</span></span>
            [0.5ex]
<span id="algorithm2.4.7.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">// </span><span id="algorithm2.4.7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">update </span>
</div>
<div id="algorithm2.4.8" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm2.4.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">8</span></span>
            Observe outcome <math id="algorithm2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and update <math id="algorithm2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{(n)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{(n)}</annotation></semantics></math> for each <math id="algorithm2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in[N]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in[N]</annotation></semantics></math> with this outcome.
</div>
<div id="algorithm2.4.9" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm2.4.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">9</span></span>
            Update <math id="algorithm2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖤</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{E}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="algorithm2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(p_{t}^{(n)},y_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(p_{t}^{(n)},y_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> as the loss of expert <math id="algorithm2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in[N]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in[N]</annotation></semantics></math>.

</div>
