<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 4.1</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any loss function <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, any calibeating algorithm with rate <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(T)</annotation></semantics></math>, and any experts algorithm with regret <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma(T)</annotation></semantics></math>, Algorithm <a href="#algorithm2" title="Algorithm 2 ‣ Expert Problem. ‣ 4 Multi-Calibeating = Calibeating + Expert Problem ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> is
<math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha(T)+\gamma(T))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha(T)+\gamma(T))</annotation></semantics></math>-calibeating.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">By the regret bound of algorithm <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖤</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{E}</annotation></semantics></math>, for any <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in[N]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in[N]</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>
<table id="S4.EGx13" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.Ex11"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\,[L_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})]\leq L_{T}(p^{(n)}_{1:T},y_{1:T})+\gamma(T)~." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo rspace="0.052em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\,[L_{T}(p_{1:T},y_{1:T})]\leq L_{T}(p^{(n)}_{1:T},y_{1:T})+\gamma(T)~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">By the calibeating rate of algorithm <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖠</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>
<table id="S4.EGx14" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.Ex12"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle L_{T}(p^{(n)}_{1:T},y_{1:T})\leq R_{T}(q^{(n)}_{1:T},y_{1:T})+\alpha(T)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>α</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle L_{T}(p^{(n)}_{1:T},y_{1:T})\leq R_{T}(q^{(n)}_{1:T},y_{1:T})+\alpha(T).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text">Combining these inequalities yields a multi-calibeating rate of <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(T)+\gamma(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(T)+\gamma(T)</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\smash{Q^{(n)}\coloneqq\{q^{(n)}_{t}:t\in[T]\}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{Q^{(n)}\coloneqq\{q^{(n)}_{t}:t\in[T]\}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the set of distinct external forecasts made by forecaster <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in[N]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in[N]</annotation></semantics></math>.
We assume <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\smash{|Q^{(n)}|=|Q|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{|Q^{(n)}|=|Q|}</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> for simplicity.<span id="footnote2" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">2</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            Our results also hold when <math id="footnote2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|Q^{(n)}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|Q^{(n)}|</annotation></semantics></math>s differ across forecasters, and the resulting bounds adapt to specific forecasters. </span></span></span>
By the regret bounds of Hedge (e.g., <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bub11</a>, Theorems 2.1 and 2.2]</cite>), and the calibeating rates in <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Corollary 3.2. ‣ 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollaries</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> and <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem4" title="Corollary 3.4. ‣ 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a>, we get the following corollaries. In contrast to the loss-oblivious property of <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Corollary 3.2. ‣ 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>, the algorithm in <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem2" title="Corollary 4.2. ‣ Expert Problem. ‣ 4 Multi-Calibeating = Calibeating + Expert Problem ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> requires a fixed <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, as the experts algorithm relies on the loss values to update.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 4.2</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any bounded proper loss <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, there exists an
algorithm with an expected multi-calibeating rate of
<math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\sqrt{T\log N}+\sqrt{|Q|KT})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\sqrt{T\log N}+\sqrt{|Q|KT})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 4.3</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any <math id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>-mixable loss <math id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., Brier and Log losses), there exists an algorithm with expected multi-calibeating rate of
<math id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log N+|Q|\log T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\log N+|Q|\log T)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We show a minimax-equivalence of the two problems.
Since now external forecasts are involved, we consider calibeating rates and expert regrets as functions of both the time round and the number of possible distinct external forecast values. Similarly to <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{(n)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{(n)}</annotation></semantics></math>, given an instance of the expert problem, let <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\smash{P^{(n)}\coloneqq\{p^{(n)}_{t}:t\in[T]\}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{P^{(n)}\coloneqq\{p^{(n)}_{t}:t\in[T]\}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the set of possible expert predictions made by expert forecaster <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\smash{n\in[N]}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{n\in[N]}</annotation></semantics></math>. We have the following theorem.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 4.4</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any proper loss <math id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>,
suppose there exist functions <math id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi,\lambda:\mathbb{Z}^{2}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi,\lambda:\mathbb{Z}^{2}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> such that for any <math id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖬</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{M}</annotation></semantics></math> ranges over all multi-calibeating algorithms.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">By
known lower bounds for expert problems
when the expert predictions can be arbitrary values <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx5" title="" class="ltx_ref">CL06</a>]</cite>, and that the lower-bound examples can be obtained when the size of distinct expert prediction values is constant, we show the following lower bounds for multi-calibeating,
matching the upper bounds.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 4.5</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There exist bounded proper losses under which the multi-calibeating rates
are at least
<math id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega(\sqrt{T\log N}+\sqrt{|Q|KT})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega(\sqrt{T\log N}+\sqrt{|Q|KT})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 4.6</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For Brier and log losses, the multi-calibeating rate of any algorithm is
at least
<math id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega(\log N+|Q|\log(T/|Q|))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega(\log N+|Q|\log(T/|Q|))</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we consider the problem of achieving simultaneous calibeating and calibration.
Existing approaches focus on the Brier loss. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx8" title="" class="ltx_ref">FH23</a>]</cite> obtain simultaneous rates of <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\smash{\tilde{O}(|Q|^{\frac{2}{K+1}}T^{\frac{K-1}{K+1}}))}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo fence="true" rspace="0em">OPEN</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>O</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{\tilde{O}(|Q|^{\frac{2}{K+1}}T^{\frac{K-1}{K+1}}))}</annotation></semantics></math> via bin refinement and stochastic fixed-point methods, while <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee+22</a>]</cite> obtain <math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\smash{\tilde{O}(\sqrt{|Q|}(\log N)^{\frac{1}{4}}T^{\frac{3}{4}})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>O</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{\tilde{O}(\sqrt{|Q|}(\log N)^{\frac{1}{4}}T^{\frac{3}{4}})}</annotation></semantics></math> in the binary case after parameter tuning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We focus on the Brier loss and provide new and improved bounds for simultaneous calibeating and calibration. Specifically, we provide a meta-algorithm (Algorithm <a href="#algorithm3" title="Algorithm 3 ‣ Interpolating between calibration and multi-calibeating. ‣ 5.1 Algorithm ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>) which, for any given external reference algorithm <math id="S5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, keeps careful track of the losses of <math id="S5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> while ensuring calibration.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 5.1</span></span><span id="S5.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For Brier loss, any <math id="S5.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, and any reference algorithm <math id="S5.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, <a href="#algorithm3" title="In Interpolating between calibration and multi-calibeating. ‣ 5.1 Algorithm ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> simultaneously guarantees an expected regret of at most <math id="S5.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\varepsilon^{2}T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\varepsilon^{2}T)</annotation></semantics></math> compared to <math id="S5.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, and a calibration rate of at most <math id="S5.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{K,\log T}(\sqrt{T}+\frac{1}{\varepsilon^{K-1}}\log\frac{1}{\varepsilon}+\varepsilon^{2}T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>T</mi></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>ε</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{K,\log T}(\sqrt{T}+\frac{1}{\varepsilon^{K-1}}\log\frac{1}{\varepsilon}+\varepsilon^{2}T)</annotation></semantics></math> with high probability.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Here, the <math id="S5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{K,\log T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{K,\log T}</annotation></semantics></math> notation hides a factor polynomial in <math id="S5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log T</annotation></semantics></math> for readability.
We hide the <math id="S5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log T</annotation></semantics></math> factors because for the calibration error, the dominant dependence in <math id="S5.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> is polynomial,
and we hide the <math id="S5.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> factors because the bounds degenerate to the trivial <math id="S5.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(T)</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="S5.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> gets larger and larger.
The bounds from previous works are also polynomial in <math id="S5.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> be a multi-calibeating algorithm from the previous sections.
With <math id="S5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon=\sqrt{\frac{\log T}{T}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mi>T</mi></mfrac></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon=\sqrt{\frac{\log T}{T}}</annotation></semantics></math>, for <math id="S5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math>,
we obtain the optimal calibeating rate, improving the polynomial-in-<math id="S5.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> dependence in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx8" title="" class="ltx_ref">FH23</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 5.2</span></span><span id="S5.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For Brier loss with binary outcomes, there is an algorithm with an expected multi-calibeating rate of at most <math id="S5.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log N+|Q|\log T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\log N+|Q|\log T)</annotation></semantics></math>, and a calibration rate of at most <math id="S5.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{K,\log T}(\sqrt{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mi>T</mi></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{K,\log T}(\sqrt{T})</annotation></semantics></math> with high probability.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p5.1" class="ltx_p">With <math id="S5.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon=(\frac{\log T}{T})^{\frac{1}{K+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon=(\frac{\log T}{T})^{\frac{1}{K+1}}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S5.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math>, we achieve the same calibration rate as in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fis+25</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx8" title="" class="ltx_ref">FH23</a>]</cite>, and drop the <math id="S5.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|Q|-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|Q|-</annotation></semantics></math>dependence in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx8" title="" class="ltx_ref">FH23</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 5.3</span></span><span id="S5.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For Brier loss and <math id="S5.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math> outcomes, there is an algorithm with an expected multi-calibeating rate of at most <math id="S5.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{K,\log T}(\log N+|Q|+T^{\frac{K-1}{K+1}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{K,\log T}(\log N+|Q|+T^{\frac{K-1}{K+1}})</annotation></semantics></math>, and a calibration rate of at most <math id="S5.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{K,\log T}(T^{\frac{K-1}{K+1}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{K,\log T}(T^{\frac{K-1}{K+1}})</annotation></semantics></math> with high probability.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p6.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="S5.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math> outcomes, we can also lower the multi-calibeating rate at the cost of raising the calibration rate, by choosing a different <math id="S5.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 5.4</span></span><span id="S5.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For Brier loss and <math id="S5.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math> outcomes, for any <math id="S5.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in(\frac{K-3}{K-1},\frac{K-1}{K+1}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in(\frac{K-3}{K-1},\frac{K-1}{K+1}]</annotation></semantics></math>, there is an algorithm with expected multi-calibeating rate of at most <math id="S5.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{K,\log T}(\log N+|Q|+T^{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{K,\log T}(\log N+|Q|+T^{x})</annotation></semantics></math>, and a calibration rate of at most <math id="S5.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\smash{O_{K,\log T}(T^{\frac{(K-1)(1-x)}{2}})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{O_{K,\log T}(T^{\frac{(K-1)(1-x)}{2}})}</annotation></semantics></math> with high probability.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Algorithm</h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Discretization and rounding.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To achieve calibration, it is necessary to focus on a finite set of predictions via discretization.
For that, we consider a triangulation of <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> and randomly round each prediction to a vertex of the triangulation (recall that <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> is fixed to the Brier loss in this section).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 5.5</span></span><span id="S5.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fis+25</a>]</cite>)<span id="S5.Thmtheorem5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any <math id="S5.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, there is a subset of predictions <math id="S5.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon}\subset\Delta_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒦</mi><mi>ε</mi></msup><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon}\subset\Delta_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> of size <math id="S5.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=|\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon}|=O(\sqrt{K}\,\varepsilon^{-K+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒦</mi><mi>ε</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>K</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=|\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon}|=O(\sqrt{K}\,\varepsilon^{-K+1})</annotation></semantics></math>, and a rounding scheme <math id="S5.Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{H}:\Delta_{K}\rightarrow\Delta\left(\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝖧</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒦</mi><mi>ε</mi></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{H}:\Delta_{K}\rightarrow\Delta\left(\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> that maps an arbitrary prediction <math id="S5.Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q\in\Delta_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q\in\Delta_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> to a distribution over those in <math id="S5.Thmtheorem5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒦</mi><mi>ε</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>, such that for any outcome <math id="S5.Thmtheorem5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y\in\mathcal{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\in\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="S5.Thmtheorem5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{s\sim\mathsf{H}(q)}\,[\ell(s,y)]\leq\ell(q,y)+O(\varepsilon^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>𝖧</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{s\sim\mathsf{H}(q)}\,[\ell(s,y)]\leq\ell(q,y)+O(\varepsilon^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Blum-Mansour reduction.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the connection between calibration and no-swap-regret learning, we employ the well-known reduction by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx2" title="" class="ltx_ref">BM07</a>]</cite> with the <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\log T)</annotation></semantics></math> regret online learning algorithm for Brier loss, e.g., <abbr title="" class="ltx_glossaryref ltx_missing">FTL</abbr>.
We present the algorithm and its proof in <a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 Algorithm 𝖠_BM and the proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 5.6</span></span><span id="S5.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There is an online algorithm <math id="S5.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{BM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝖠</mi><mi>BM</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{BM}}</annotation></semantics></math> that, in each step <math id="S5.Thmtheorem6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[T]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[T]</annotation></semantics></math>, first predicts an <math id="S5.Thmtheorem6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times M</annotation></semantics></math> column-stochastic matrix <math id="S5.Thmtheorem6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, and then observes outcome <math id="S5.Thmtheorem6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and a distribution <math id="S5.Thmtheorem6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{t}\in\Delta(\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒦</mi><mi>ε</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{t}\in\Delta(\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon})</annotation></semantics></math>, such that for any transformation <math id="S5.Thmtheorem6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma:\Delta_{K}\rightarrow\Delta_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma:\Delta_{K}\rightarrow\Delta_{K}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S5.EGx18" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S5.Ex16"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S5.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\sum_{t\in[T]}\mathbb{E}_{p_{t}\sim A_{t}\pi_{t}}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})\leq\sum_{t\in[T]}\mathbb{E}_{p_{t}^{\prime}\sim\pi_{t}}\ell(\sigma(p_{t}^{\prime}),y_{t})+O\left(M\log T+\varepsilon^{2}T\right)~." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.052em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\sum_{t\in[T]}\mathbb{E}_{p_{t}\sim A_{t}\pi_{t}}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})\leq\sum_{t\in[T]}\mathbb{E}_{p_{t}^{\prime}\sim\pi_{t}}\ell(\sigma(p_{t}^{\prime}),y_{t})+O\left(M\log T+\varepsilon^{2}T\right)~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Intuitively, we may interpret the column-stochastic matrix <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> from algorithm <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{BM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝖠</mi><mi>BM</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{BM}}</annotation></semantics></math> as a suggested remapping from any prediction, so that for any sequence of outcomes <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and distributions of predictions <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, the remapped/calibrated predictions are competitive against the best remapping <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>
in hindsight.
The standard approach is then to sample a randomized prediction from the stationary distribution of
<math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> (but we will do this step later after mixing <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> with another remapping matrix).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Interpolating between calibration and multi-calibeating.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Besides achieving small swap regret and calibration rate, we also want to follow the reference prediction <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> from algorithm <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> to be competitive against this reference algorithm.
Observe that following the reference prediction corresponds to remapping every prediction to <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, which can be captured by a remapping matrix <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\smash{B_{t}=(b_{t},b_{t},\dots,b_{t})\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times M}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{B_{t}=(b_{t},b_{t},\dots,b_{t})\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times M}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
To hedge between these two factors, we resort to a lopsided two-expert algorithm <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{lopsided}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝖠</mi><mi>lopsided</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{lopsided}}</annotation></semantics></math> to obtain a weight <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{t}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{t}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, and take a linear combination <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{t}=w_{t}A_{t}+(1-w_{t})B_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{t}=w_{t}A_{t}+(1-w_{t})B_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> as the aggregated remapping.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 5.7</span></span><span id="S5.Thmtheorem7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx22" title="" class="ltx_ref">SNL14</a>]</cite>)<span id="S5.Thmtheorem7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.Thmtheorem7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.Thmtheorem7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmtheorem7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There is an algorithm <math id="S5.Thmtheorem7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{lopsided}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝖠</mi><mi>lopsided</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{lopsided}}</annotation></semantics></math> for the expert problem with two experts, such that the expected regret w.r.t. expert <math id="S5.Thmtheorem7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> is at most <math id="S5.Thmtheorem7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\sqrt{T\log T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\sqrt{T\log T})</annotation></semantics></math>, and the expected regret w.r.t. expert <math id="S5.Thmtheorem7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> is at most <math id="S5.Thmtheorem7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(1)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we sample a prediction from the stationary distribution of <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, as shown in <a href="#algorithm3" title="In Interpolating between calibration and multi-calibeating. ‣ 5.1 Algorithm ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.</p>
</div>

                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm3.4.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2</span></span>

</div>
<div id="algorithm3.4.3" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> <span id="algorithm3.4.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">// </span><span id="algorithm3.4.3.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">prediction </span>
</div>
<div id="algorithm3.4.4" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>

</div>
<div id="algorithm3.4.5" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm3.4.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">5</span></span>
              Round algorithm <math id="algorithm3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>’s prediction with <math id="algorithm3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖧</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{H}</annotation></semantics></math> to get <math id="algorithm3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{t}\in\Delta(\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒦</mi><mi>ε</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{t}\in\Delta(\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon})</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="algorithm3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}=(b_{t},\dots,b_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}=(b_{t},\dots,b_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.
</div>
<div id="algorithm3.4.6" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm3.4.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">6</span></span>

</div>
<div id="algorithm3.4.7" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm3.4.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">7</span></span>
              Let <math id="algorithm3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{t}=w_{t}A_{t}+(1-w_{t})B_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{t}=w_{t}A_{t}+(1-w_{t})B_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="algorithm3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{t}\in\Delta_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{t}\in\Delta_{M}</annotation></semantics></math> be its stationary distribution, i.e., <math id="algorithm3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{t}=C_{t}\pi_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{t}=C_{t}\pi_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. 
</div>
<div id="algorithm3.4.8" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm3.4.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">8</span></span>
              Predict <math id="algorithm3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}\sim\pi_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}\sim\pi_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. 
</div>
<div id="algorithm3.4.9" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm3.4.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">9</span></span>
              [0.5ex]
<span id="algorithm3.4.9.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">// </span><span id="algorithm3.4.9.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">update </span>
</div>
<div id="algorithm3.4.10" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm3.4.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">10</span></span>
              Observe outcome <math id="algorithm3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. 
</div>
<div id="algorithm3.4.11" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm3.4.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">11</span></span>
              Update <math id="algorithm3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{BM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝖠</mi><mi>BM</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{BM}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="algorithm3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> based on <math id="algorithm3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="algorithm3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> (applicable to the former).
</div>
<div id="algorithm3.4.12" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm3.4.12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">12</span></span>
              Update <math id="algorithm3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{lopsided}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝖠</mi><mi>lopsided</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{lopsided}}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="algorithm3.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{z\sim A_{t}\pi_{t}}\ell(z,y_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{z\sim A_{t}\pi_{t}}\ell(z,y_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="algorithm3.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{z\sim b_{t}}\ell(z,y_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{z\sim b_{t}}\ell(z,y_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> as the losses of experts 1 and 2.
</div>

<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Analysis: Proof of a weaker version of <a href="#S5.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 5.1. ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a></h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We will prove a weaker guarantee of pseudo-calibration due to space constraints and defer the rest of the proof to <a href="#A3.SS4" title="C.4 Concentration arguments to finish the proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.4</span></a>.
By definition, the expected cumulative loss of <a href="#algorithm3" title="In Interpolating between calibration and multi-calibeating. ‣ 5.1 Algorithm ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Algorithm</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> is</p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S5.E6.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}_{b_{1:T}}\bigg[\sum_{t\in[T]}\mathbb{E}_{z_{t}\sim b_{t}}\ell(z_{t},y_{t})\bigg]+O(1)~." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">[</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="2.100em" minsize="2.100em">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>O</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="0.052em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}_{b_{1:T}}\bigg[\sum_{t\in[T]}\mathbb{E}_{z_{t}\sim b_{t}}\ell(z_{t},y_{t})\bigg]+O(1)~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Regret w.r.t. <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recall that <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is obtained by rounding the prediction from <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> with rounding algorithm <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖧</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{H}</annotation></semantics></math>.
By the <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\varepsilon^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\varepsilon^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> rounding error bound of <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖧</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{H}</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#S5.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma 5.5 ([]). ‣ Discretization and rounding. ‣ 5.1 Algorithm ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.5</span></a>) and <a href="#S5.E6" title="In 5.2 Analysis: Proof of a weaker version of ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, the regret w.r.t. the reference algorithm <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> is at most <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\varepsilon^{2}T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\varepsilon^{2}T)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Pseudo-calibration.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We will prove a weaker guarantee that</p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.Ex20.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed"
