</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This follows from <a href="#S5.E5" title="In 5.2 Analysis: Proof of a weaker version of ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, the guarantee of <abbr title="" class="ltx_glossaryref ltx_missing">BM</abbr> reduction (<a href="#S5.Thmtheorem6" title="Lemma 5.6. ‣ Blum-Mansour reduction. ‣ 5.1 Algorithm ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a>), and that <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=O(\sqrt{K}\varepsilon^{-K+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>K</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=O(\sqrt{K}\varepsilon^{-K+1})</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#S5.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma 5.5 ([]). ‣ Discretization and rounding. ‣ 5.1 Algorithm ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.5</span></a>).
It is weaker than the original statement as the choice of <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> does not depend on the realization of randomness of the algorithm.
By contrast, the original statement allows choosing <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> based on the realization of randomness.
We defer this concentration argument to <a href="#A3.SS4" title="C.4 Concentration arguments to finish the proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We have revisited calibeating through the lens of online learning and developed a reduction-based framework that connects calibeating and its extensions to standard online-learning notions. This
viewpoint
enables us to recover and sharpen existing results, extend them to general proper scoring losses, and deliver new matching lower bounds,
in a unified and modular way.
A natural direction for future work is to
push this approach further—both to identify additional achievable guarantees and to improve online forecasting more broadly.
Another open question is whether one can simultaneously achieve an <math id="S6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(|Q|\log T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(|Q|\log T)</annotation></semantics></math> calibeating rate and <math id="S6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\smash{\tilde{O}(T^{\frac{1}{3}})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>O</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\smash{\tilde{O}(T^{\frac{1}{3}})}</annotation></semantics></math> calibration for the binary case, matching the best known bounds for each objective, and whether analogous simultaneous guarantees
hold
beyond the Brier loss. In fact, the meta-algorithm developed in <a href="#S5" title="5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> suggests a general recipe that may apply more broadly. Whenever one can identify an appropriate discretization of the prediction space, a compatible rounding scheme with controlled loss guarantees, and a mechanism for upgrading pseudo-swap regret to true swap regret, the same framework should yield analogous extensions to other loss functions.</p>
</div>
</section>

<p id="A1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">By Yao’s minimax principle, (<a href="#S3.E3" title="Eq. 3 ‣ Theorem 3.5. ‣ 3 Calibeating = No-Regret Learning ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>) implies that, for any <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>,

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\min_{\mathsf{D}}\mathbb{E}_{y_{1:T}\sim\mathrm{S}_{T}}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell\left(p_{t},y_{t}\right)-\min_{p\in\Delta_{K}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell\left(p,y_{t}\right)\right]\geq\beta(T)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder><mi>min</mi><mi>𝖣</mi></munder><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>y</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∼</mo><mi>S</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover></mstyle><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover></mstyle><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>β</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\min_{\mathsf{D}}\mathbb{E}_{y_{1:T}\sim\mathrm{S}_{T}}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell\left(p_{t},y_{t}\right)-\min_{p\in\Delta_{K}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell\left(p,y_{t}\right)\right]\geq\beta(T),</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A1.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">where the minimum is over deterministic online algorithms <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖣</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{D}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">For any <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> and the corresponding <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{q}</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{S}_{q}=\mathrm{S}_{T_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{S}_{q}=\mathrm{S}_{T_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> be the distribution guaranteed by (<a href="#A1.E7" title="Eq. 7 ‣ Proof. ‣ A.1 Proof of ‣ Appendix A Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>) at horizon <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{q}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Define the following distribution <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{S}</annotation></semantics></math> over pairs<math id="A1.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(q_{1:T},y_{1:T})\in(Q\times\mathcal{E})^{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q_{1:T},y_{1:T})\in(Q\times\mathcal{E})^{T}</annotation></semantics></math> as follows:</span></p>
<ol id="A1.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Choose disjoint index sets <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathcal{I}_{q}\}_{q\in Q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathcal{I}_{q}\}_{q\in Q}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}_{q}\subseteq[T]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}_{q}\subseteq[T]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathcal{I}_{q}|=T_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathcal{I}_{q}|=T_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\cup_{q\in Q}\mathcal{I}_{q}=[T]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cup_{q\in Q}\mathcal{I}_{q}=[T]</annotation></semantics></math>. Set <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}=q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}=q</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in\mathcal{I}_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in\mathcal{I}_{q}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q\in Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q\in Q</annotation></semantics></math>, denote the subsequence of outcomes <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>s that <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in\mathcal{I}_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in\mathcal{I}_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> to be <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{\mathcal{I}_{q}}=(y_{t})_{t\in\mathcal{I}_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{\mathcal{I}_{q}}=(y_{t})_{t\in\mathcal{I}_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Independently sample <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{\mathcal{I}_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{\mathcal{I}_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> according to <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{S}_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{S}_{q}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>

<p id="A1.SS1.p4.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p4.3.1" class="ltx_text">Therefore, since a randomized algorithm <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> is a probability distribution over deterministic algorithms, it holds that</span></p>

<p id="A1.SS1.p4.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p4.4.1" class="ltx_text">Choosing balanced <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{q}\in\{\lfloor T/|Q|\rfloor,\lceil T/|Q|\rceil\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌊</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌋</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌈</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌉</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{q}\in\{\lfloor T/|Q|\rfloor,\lceil T/|Q|\rceil\}</annotation></semantics></math> completes the proof.
∎</span></p>

<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Proof of <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 4.4. ‣ Expert Problem. ‣ 4 Multi-Calibeating = Calibeating + Expert Problem ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a></h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">See <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 4.4. ‣ Expert Problem. ‣ 4 Multi-Calibeating = Calibeating + Expert Problem ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a></p>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">First, for any realization of expert predictions <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{p^{(n)}_{t}\}_{t\in[T],n\in[N]}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{p^{(n)}_{t}\}_{t\in[T],n\in[N]}</annotation></semantics></math> and outcomes <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="y_{1:T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{(n)}_{t}=p^{(n)}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation By <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1" title="Definition 2.1. ‣ 2 Model ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Definition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>,</span></p>

<tbody id="A2.Ex32"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex32.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})-\min_{n\in[N]}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p^{(n)}_{t},y_{t})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mmultiscripts><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><mprescripts></mprescripts><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow></mmultiscripts></mstyle><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})-\min_{n\in[N]}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p^{(n)}_{t},y_{t}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text">and multi-calibeating inherits the lower bound of the expert problem.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Second, consider the instances where <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{(n)}_{t}=q_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{(n)}_{t}=q_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[T]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[T]</annotation></semantics></math>, which is equivalent to beating only one external forecaster. Therefore, multi-calibeating inherits the lower bound of the calibeating problem. This completes the proof.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Omitted Proofs in <a href="#S5" title="5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a></h2>

<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Proof of <a href="#S5.Thmtheorem4" title="Corollary 5.4. ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a></h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">See <a href="#S5.Thmtheorem4" title="Corollary 5.4. ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon^{2}T=T^{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>ε</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon^{2}T=T^{x}</annotation></semantics></math>, then the calibeating rate is <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(|Q^{(n)}|\log T+T^{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(|Q^{(n)}|\log T+T^{x})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon=T^{\frac{x-1}{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon=T^{\frac{x-1}{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The corresponding calibration error is of the order <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\sqrt{T\log T}+T^{\frac{(K-1)(1-x)}{2}}\log T+T^{x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\sqrt{T\log T}+T^{\frac{(K-1)(1-x)}{2}}\log T+T^{x})</annotation></semantics></math>, which always has greater order than the regret. As the order of calibration error is optimized when <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x=\frac{(K-1)(1-x)}{2}=\frac{K-1}{K+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x=\frac{(K-1)(1-x)}{2}=\frac{K-1}{K+1}</annotation></semantics></math>, we consider smaller <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> with higher <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{\frac{(K-1)(1-x)}{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>T</mi><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{\frac{(K-1)(1-x)}{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> term. The tradeoff follows by solving <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{\frac{(K-1)(1-x)}{2}}&lt;T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{\frac{(K-1)(1-x)}{2}}&lt;T</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Algorithm <math id="A3.SS2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{BM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝖠</mi><mi>BM</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}_{\mathrm{BM}}</annotation></semantics></math> and the proof of <a href="#S5.Thmtheorem6" title="Lemma 5.6. ‣ Blum-Mansour reduction. ‣ 5.1 Algorithm ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a></h3>

</div>

            Output <math id="algorithm4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}=(\mathsf{H}(q^{(1)}_{t}),\dots,\mathsf{H}(q^{(M)}_{t}))\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝖧</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>𝖧</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}=(\mathsf{H}(q^{(1)}_{t}),\dots,\mathsf{H}(q^{(M)}_{t}))\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times M}</annotation></semantics></math>.
</div>
<div id="algorithm4.4.8" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm4.4.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">7</span></span>
            [1.5ex]
<span id="algorithm4.4.8.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">// </span><span id="algorithm4.4.8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">update </span>
</div>
<div id="algorithm4.4.9" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm4.4.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">8</span></span>
            Receive feedback tuple <math id="algorithm4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(y_{t},\pi_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(y_{t},\pi_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.
</div>
<div id="algorithm4.4.10" class="ltx_listingline"> <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:1px;height:100%;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="algorithm4.4.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">9</span></span>
            Update Algorithm <math id="algorithm4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝖠</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math> with loss function <math id="algorithm4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{t}(i)\ell(\cdot,y_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{t}(i)\ell(\cdot,y_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.
</div>

</figure>

<div id="A3.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Denote <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon}\coloneqq\{z_{1},\dots,z_{M}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒦</mi><mi>ε</mi></msup><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{K}^{\varepsilon}\coloneqq\{z_{1},\dots,z_{M}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. For any <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\in[M]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\in[M]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(z_{j})\in\Delta_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(z_{j})\in\Delta_{K}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>

<p id="A3.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">for some positive constants <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{1},C_{2}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{1},C_{2}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a)</annotation></semantics></math> follows from the definition of the rounding scheme and the upper bound of the rounding error (<a href="#S5.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma 5.5 ([]). ‣ Discretization and rounding. ‣ 5.1 Algorithm ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.5</span></a>);
<math id="A3.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(b)</annotation></semantics></math> holds by that <abbr title="" class="ltx_glossaryref ltx_missing">FTL</abbr> has a regret of <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\log T)</annotation></semantics></math> under the Brier loss.</span></p>

<p id="A3.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">where in the last inequality, we use <math id="A3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=O(\frac{\sqrt{K}}{\varepsilon^{K-1}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mi>K</mi></msqrt><msup><mi>ε</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=O(\frac{\sqrt{K}}{\varepsilon^{K-1}})</annotation></semantics></math> in <a href="#S5.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma 5.5 ([]). ‣ Discretization and rounding. ‣ 5.1 Algorithm ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.5</span></a>.
∎</span></p>

<section id="A3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.4 </span>Concentration arguments to finish the proof of <a href="#S5.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 5.1. ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a></h3>

<div id="A3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We finish the proof of <a href="#S5.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 5.1. ‣ 5 Calibeating and Calibration at the Same Time ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a> by upper-bounding the true calibration error using bounds of the pseudo-calibration error.
For convenience,
denote the pseudo-calibration error under an algorithm <math id="A3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖠</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> to be <math id="A3.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\widetilde{K}_{T}\coloneqq\min_{\sigma:\Delta_{K}\rightarrow\Delta_{K}}\mathbb{E}_{p_{t}\sim\mathsf{A}}\left[\sum^{T}_{t=1}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})-\sum^{T}_{t=1}\ell(\sigma(p_{t}),y_{t})\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></msub><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mi>𝖠</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><msubsup><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">−</mo><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{K}_{T}\coloneqq\min_{\sigma:\Delta_{K}\rightarrow\Delta_{K}}\mathbb{E}_{p_{t}\sim\mathsf{A}}\left[\sum^{T}_{t=1}\ell(p_{t},y_{t})-\sum^{T}_{t=1}\ell(\sigma(p_{t}),y_{t})\right]</annotation></semantics></math>.
The following lemma is a multiclass extension of Theorem 3 in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx18" title="" class="ltx_ref">LSS25</a>]</cite>, relating <math id="A3.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{K}_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{K}_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> to the calibration error.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma C.1</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For the Brier loss, for discretization with size <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> and an algorithm <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖠</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}</annotation></semantics></math> that always predicts the discretization grid points, with probability at least <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math> over the randomness in <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝖠</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{A}</annotation></semantics></math>’s predictions <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1},\dots,p_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1},\dots,p_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>
<table id="A3.EGx30" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex42"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<section id="A3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.5 </span>Proof of <a href="#A3.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma C.1. ‣ C.4 Concentration arguments to finish the proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a></h3>

<div id="A3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first note the following fact on the closed-form of <math id="A3.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{K}_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{K}_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_fact">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Fact C.2</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>

<p id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the Brier losses, the calibration error under prediction sequence <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{1:T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1:T}</annotation></semantics></math> and outcome sequence <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="y_{1:T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{1:T}</annotation></semantics></math> is</p>

<div id="A3.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Denote the <math id="A3.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>th grid point by <math id="A3.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> in the discretization, and <math id="A3.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho^{p}_{T}(k)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>p</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho^{p}_{T}(k)</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A3.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho^{i}(k)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho^{i}(k)</annotation></semantics></math> for simplicity.
For any <math id="A3.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in[K]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in[K]</annotation></semantics></math>, let</p>
<table id="A3.EGx34" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex47"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex47.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle K_{T}(k)\coloneq\sum_{i\in[M]}\sum^{T}_{t=1}\mathbf{1}\{p_{t}=z_{i}\}\left(z_{i}(k)-\rho^{i}(k)\right)^{2}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≔</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover></mstyle><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle K_{T}(k)\coloneq\sum_{i\in[M]}\sum^{T}_{t=1}\mathbf{1}\{p_{t}=z_{i}\}\left(z_{i}(k)-\rho^{i}(k)\right)^{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS5.p2.2" class="ltx_p">and</p>
<table id="A3.EGx35" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex48"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex48.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\widetilde{K}_{T}(k)\coloneqq\sum_{i\in[M]}\sum^{T}_{t=1}P_{t}(z_{i})(z_{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k))^{2}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\widetilde{K}_{T}(k)\coloneqq\sum_{i\in[M]}\sum^{T}_{t=1}P_{t}(z_{i})(z_{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k))^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We have the following lemma.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma C.3</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">With probability at least <math id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{T}(k)\leq 6\widetilde{K}_{T}(k)+96M\log\frac{4M}{\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>96</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mi>δ</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{T}(k)\leq 6\widetilde{K}_{T}(k)+96M\log\frac{4M}{\delta}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Then, with a union bound across <math id="A3.SS5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in[K]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in[K]</annotation></semantics></math>, with probability at least <math id="A3.SS5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</p>
<table id="A3.EGx36" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex49"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex49.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle K_{T}=\sum^{K}_{k=1}K_{T}(k)\leq\sum^{K}_{k=1}\left(6\widetilde{K}_{T}(k)+96M\log\frac{4MK}{\delta}\right)=6\widetilde{K}_{T}+96MK\log\frac{4MK}{\delta}." display="inline" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>96</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo K_{T}=\sum^{K}_{k=1}K_{T}(k)\leq\sum^{K}_{k=1}\left(6\widetilde{K}_{T}(k)+96M\log\frac{4MK}{\delta}\right)=6\widetilde{K}_{T}+96MK\log\frac{4MK}{\delta}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</section>
<section id="A3.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.6 </span>Proof of <a href="#A3.Thmtheorem3" title="Lemma C.3. ‣ C.5 Proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a></h3>

<div id="A3.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">See <a href="#A3.Thmtheorem3" title="Lemma C.3. ‣ C.5 Proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">While the proof of <a href="#A3.Thmtheorem3" title="Lemma C.3. ‣ C.5 Proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a> follows almost exactly as the proof of Theorem 3 in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx18" title="" class="ltx_ref">LSS25</a>]</cite>, we include it here for completeness.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of <a href="#A3.Thmtheorem3" title="Lemma C.3. ‣ C.5 Proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="A3.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">The proof relies on the following version of Freedman’s inequality.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma C.4</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bey+11</a>]</cite>)<span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{X_{i}\}^{n}_{i=1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{X_{i}\}^{n}_{i=1}</annotation></semantics></math> be a martingale difference sequence adapted to the filtration <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{1}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal{F}_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">⊆</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.1389em">⋯</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em">⊆</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{1}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal{F}_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|X_{i}\right|\leq B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|X_{i}\right|\leq B</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in[n]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in[n]</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> is a fixed constant. Define <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\left[X_{i}^{2}\mid\mathcal{F}_{i-1}\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">:=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\left[X_{i}^{2}\mid\mathcal{F}_{i-1}\right]</annotation></semantics></math>. Then, for any fixed <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu\in\left[0,\frac{1}{B}\right],\delta\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>B</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu\in\left[0,\frac{1}{B}\right],\delta\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, with probability at least <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>
<table id="A3.EGx37" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex50"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex50.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_{i}\right|\leq\mu\mathcal{V}+\frac{\log\frac{2}{\delta}}{\mu}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover></mstyle><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mi>δ</mi></mfrac></mrow><mi>μ</mi></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_{i}\right|\leq\mu\mathcal{V}+\frac{\log\frac{2}{\delta}}{\mu}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix <math id="A3.SS6.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in[M]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in[M]</annotation></semantics></math> and define the martingale difference sequence <math id="A3.SS6.p4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="X_{t}\coloneqq y_{t}(k)(P_{t}(i)-\mathbf{1}\{p_{t}=z_{i}\})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{t}\coloneqq y_{t}(k)(P_{t}(i)-\mathbf{1}\{p_{t}=z_{i}\})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS6.p4.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="Y_{t}\coloneqq P_{t}(i)-\mathbf{1}\{p_{t}=z_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{t}\coloneqq P_{t}(i)-\mathbf{1}\{p_{t}=z_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Observe that <math id="A3.SS6.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|X_{t}|\leq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|X_{t}|\leq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS6.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|Y_{t}|\leq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|Y_{t}|\leq 1</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A3.SS6.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. Fix <math id="A3.SS6.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{i}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{i}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. <div id="A3.SS6.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Combining both bounds, we have shown that for a fixed <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{i}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{i}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\rho^{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k)|\leq 2\mu_{i}+\frac{\log\frac{4}{\delta}}{\mu_{i}\sum^{T}_{t=1}P_{t}(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mi>δ</mi></mfrac></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><msubsup><mo maxsize="0.700em" minsize="0.700em" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\rho^{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k)|\leq 2\mu_{i}+\frac{\log\frac{4}{\delta}}{\mu_{i}\sum^{T}_{t=1}P_{t}(i)}</annotation></semantics></math> holds with probability at least <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math>. Taking a union bound over all <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, with probability <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, the following holds simultaneously for all <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<p id="A3.SS6.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">Consider the function <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(\mu):=\mu+\frac{a}{\mu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>μ</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(\mu):=\mu+\frac{a}{\mu}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> is a fixed constant. Clearly, <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\min_{\mu\in[0,1]}g(\mu)=2\sqrt{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mi>a</mi></msqrt></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\min_{\mu\in[0,1]}g(\mu)=2\sqrt{a}</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\leq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\leq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1+a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1+a</annotation></semantics></math> otherwise. Minimizing the bound in (<a href="#A3.E11" title="Eq. 11 ‣ Proof of . ‣ C.6 Proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>) with respect to <math id="A3.SS6.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, we obtain</span></p>

<div id="A3.SS6.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">Therefore, when <math id="A3.SS6.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{t=1}^{T}P_{t}(i)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{t=1}^{T}P_{t}(i)</annotation></semantics></math> is tiny, which is possible if algorithm <math id="A3.SS6.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> does not allocate enough probability mass to the index <math id="A3.SS6.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, the bound obtained is large making it much worse than the trivial bound <math id="A3.SS6.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|\rho^{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k)\right|\leq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\rho^{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k)\right|\leq 1</annotation></semantics></math> which follows since <math id="A3.SS6.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho^{i}(k),\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k)\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho^{i}(k),\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k)\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> by definition. Based on this reasoning, we define the set</span></p>

<p id="A3.SS6.p7.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p7.2.1" class="ltx_text">and let <math id="A3.SS6.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathcal{I}}\coloneqq[M]\setminus\mathcal{I}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∖</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathcal{I}}\coloneqq[M]\setminus\mathcal{I}</annotation></semantics></math>. We bound <math id="A3.SS6.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\rho^{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k))^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\rho^{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k))^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> as</span></p>
<table id="A3.EGx45" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.E13"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\left(\rho^{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k)\right)^{2}\leq\begin{cases}\frac{16\log\frac{4M}{\delta}}{\sum_{t=1}^{T}P_{t}(i)}&amp;\text{ if }i\in\mathcal{I},\\
1&amp;\text{ otherwise. }\end{cases}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mfrac><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mi>δ</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><msubsup><mo maxsize="0.700em" minsize="0.700em" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext> if </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mn>1</mn></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mtext> otherwise.</mtext></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\left(\rho^{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k)\right)^{2}\leq\begin{cases}\frac{16\log\frac{4M}{\delta}}{\sum_{t=1}^{T}P_{t}(i)}&amp;\text{ if }i\in\mathcal{I},\\
1&amp;\text{ otherwise. }\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A3.SS6.p9.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p9.4.1" class="ltx_text">where (a) follows by substituting the bounds from (<a href="#A3.E13" title="Eq. 13 ‣ Proof of . ‣ C.6 Proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>) and (<a href="#A3.E14" title="Eq. 14 ‣ Proof of . ‣ C.6 Proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>); while (b) follows since by the definition of <math id="A3.SS6.p9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}</annotation></semantics></math> in (<a href="#A3.E12" title="Eq. 12 ‣ Proof of . ‣ C.6 Proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>), we have <math id="A3.SS6.p9.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{\log\frac{4M}{\delta}\sum_{\tau=1}^{T}P_{\tau}(i)}\leq\sum_{\tau=1}^{T}P_{\tau}(i)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mi>δ</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></msqrt><mo rspace="0.111em">≤</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{\log\frac{4M}{\delta}\sum_{\tau=1}^{T}P_{\tau}(i)}\leq\sum_{\tau=1}^{T}P_{\tau}(i)</annotation></semantics></math>. Next, we bound <math id="A3.SS6.p9.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> as</span></p>

<p id="A3.SS6.p9.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS6.p9.5.1" class="ltx_text">where (a) follows by substituting the bounds from (<a href="#A3.E13" title="Eq. 13 ‣ Proof of . ‣ C.6 Proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>) and (<a href="#A3.E14" title="Eq. 14 ‣ Proof of . ‣ C.6 Proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>); (b) follows by bounding <math id="A3.SS6.p9.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(z_{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k))^{2}\leq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(z_{i}(k)-\tilde{\rho}^{i}(k))^{2}\leq 1</annotation></semantics></math>; and (c) follows from the definition of <math id="A3.SS6.p9.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}</annotation></semantics></math> in (<a href="#A3.E12" title="Eq. 12 ‣ Proof of . ‣ C.6 Proof of ‣ Appendix C Omitted Proofs in ‣ Calibeating Made Simple" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>). Collecting the bounds on <math id="A3.SS6.p9.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS6.p9.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, we obtain</span></p>
